title: The Building Blocks of GTM Orchestration — Arman Vaziri, Ramp
talk_summary: Arman Vaziri describes how Ramp built GTM orchestration by first constructing a consistent internal data substrate (a CDP in Postgres plus vector search) and durable execution on Temporal, then layering vertical agent use-cases (pre-meeting briefs) that are later federated horizontally via a shared MCP tool layer. The core lesson is to solve one team's specific problem, expose the same tools/skills to humans and background agents, and let adoption reveal what to productionize.

takeaways.technique: Durable execution threads for agent runs
takeaways.what_they_do: Represent every agent run as a durable thread (Temporal) where each tool call and model call is an activity, so a crashed worker resumes from accumulated state instead of restarting the whole thread.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Everything is represented as a durable thread built around Temporal, representing each tool call and model call as an activity.

takeaways.technique: Scoped retrieval instead of full-corpus context
takeaways.what_they_do: Chunk and embed unstructured data (transcripts, emails, playbooks) into a vector store and combine vector + attribute + keyword search scoped to a specific account, avoiding pulling the raw corpus into agent context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: without having to pull in like the full raw corpus into agent context, um, which would also be very inefficient, very expensive.

takeaways.technique: Shared MCP tool layer for background agents and humans
takeaways.what_they_do: Expose the exact same tools/skills used by background agents through a single internal MCP endpoint so employees can build their own agents on the same substrate, and their usage reveals what to productionize.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we set up a what we call like our GT MCP, uh and this is basically just like uh a window into the same exact tools

takeaways.technique: User-editable skill library layered on system skills
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep system-level skills plus per-user custom instructions in text, so each operator can specify their preferred format and the agent composes both.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we've gone and built a skill library to allow people to customize their agents

takeaways.technique: Solve one vertical use-case, then scale horizontally
takeaways.what_they_do: Build a single team's automation end-to-end first, then reuse the data integrations and skills for adjacent teams rather than designing a grand architecture up front.
takeaways.evidence_quote: solve for one team first, then scale horizontally.

takeaways.technique: Fan-out background agents per entity on a schedule
takeaways.what_they_do: Every night fan out a set of agents that each compute per-account meeting prep using scoped tools, system skills, and user instructions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every night we're going to go and generate these things, fan out a set of agents that are going to go and compute, uh, per account
